Welcome to the iMigration app!
My name is Migri, your virtual assistant.
I'm here to help you with using the iMigration app.
This app is designed to help you navigate the complex world of immigration services!
Whether you're looking to apply for a visa, understand your rights, or find resources, I'm here to assist you every step of the way.
Let's get started!
This is the home screen where you can find all the services we offer.
You can browse through different categories such as visas, citizenship, and legal assistance.
Tap on any service to learn more about it and see if it fits your needs.
If you need help or have questions, just tap the 'Lightbulb' icon in the bottom right corner to chat with me!
Welcome to the i589 application for asylum!
This application will guide you through the process of completing and submitting your asylum application to the U.S. government.
The application is divided into several sections, each focusing on different aspects of your personal information, background, and reasons for seeking asylum.
You will be asked to provide detailed answers to various questions, as well as upload any supporting documents that may help strengthen your case.
Please take your time to read each question carefully and provide accurate and honest answers.
If you are unsure about any question or need assistance, consider consulting with one of our legal experts or support staff.
Here you need to indicate if you arrived in the U.S. in the last year.
This is important for your asylum application.
Just select "Yes" or "No." Click Confirm when you're done.
Here you need to indicate if you are from a country considered "safe" by the U.S.
This is important to know if you could have sought protection there.
Select "Yes" or "No" as applicable.
Click Confirm when you're ready.
Indicate if you are currently in the United States. This is important for your application. Use "Yes" or "No." Once you're ready, click Confirm.
Please indicate if you have applied for asylum in the United States before.
This information is important for your application.
Select "Yes" or "No" and click Confirm when you're ready.
Please indicate if you left your country because you feared harm or persecution.
This is important for your asylum application.
Select "Yes" or "No" based on your situation.
Click Confirm when you're done.
Here you need to indicate if the harm you suffered was for any of these reasons.
Choose all that apply: nationality, political opinion, race, religion, or social group.
If your reason is not on the list, select "Other" and specify.
This is important for your asylum application.

Here you need to indicate if the harm you suffered was caused by your government or by people they could not control. This is important for your asylum application. Select "Yes" or "No" based on your situation. Click Confirm when you're done.
Woohoo! You qualify to apply for asylum!
Now, let's get started with your application.
First, we will gather some personal information about you.
Remember, you can change and correct the information at any time.
Press the 'Start' button when you are ready to begin.
Let's start by getting your contact information.
Please provide your phone number and email address.
This information will help us stay in touch with you about your application.
Both fields are optional, but providing them is recommended.
Click Confirm when you are ready to continue.
Here, simply indicate your sex at birth as it appears on your birth certificate.
You can scroll up and down on the calendar to change the month, day, and year. Click Confirm when you are ready.
Enter the city where you were born. This is important for your asylum application.
Then, write the country where you were born. Make sure the information is correct.
Click Confirm when you have finished.
Here, you need to indicate your nationality at birth and your current nationality.
The nationality at birth is what appears on your birth certificate.
The current nationality is the citizenship you hold at this moment.
Make sure to be accurate, as this information is important for your application.
Here you need to provide additional information about your ethnicity and religion.
Indicate your race, ethnicity, or tribal group as you identify.
Also, state what your religion is.
This information will help better understand your situation and experiences.
Click Confirm when you have finished.
First, you must indicate whether you have a birth certificate.
If you have one, upload a copy here.
This is important for your application.
Click 'Confirm' when you are done.
If you have other names or aliases that you use or have used, indicate them here.
If you have other names or aliases that you use regularly, like a maiden name, a middle name, or a name in another language, indicate them here.
Here you need to put your first and last name as they appear on your passport or ID document.
Indicate your native language in the "Native language" field.
If you speak a specific dialect, mention it as well.
This helps us better understand your communication and needs.
Click Confirm when you are done.
Indicate which other languages you speak fluently. This is important for your application.
Write the languages in the space provided. Make sure to be specific and clear.
When you are finished, click Confirm.
We are ready to start your application. Remember that you can change and correct the information at any time.
In this section, tell us if you have a passport. This is important for your asylum application.
If you have a passport, provide the number and the country that issued it.
If you don't have one, select "No" and continue.
Remember that this information helps verify your identity. Thank you!
In this section, indicate if you have an Alien Registration Number (A-Number).
This number starts with the letter "A" followed by 8 or 9 digits (example: A123456789).
You can find it in documents from immigration offices.
If you have one, write it in the corresponding field.
Click Confirm when you are ready.
To continue, let us know if you have a Social Security Number (SSN).
This is important for your application.
If you have one, make sure to write it correctly.
If you do not have an SSN, simply select "No."
Click Confirm when you are ready.
Now we need to know if you have a USCIS online account number.
This number is given to you when you create an account on the USCIS website.
You can also find it in the notifications you received from the immigration office.
Remember, this number is different from your Alien Number (A-number).
If you have it, please write it in the following field.
Click Confirm when you're done.
In this section, let us know if you have been or are currently in an immigration court process.
There are three options to choose from:

1. You are currently in a process.
2. You were in a process before.
3. You have never been in a process.
Make sure to select the option that best describes your situation. This is important for your application. Click Confirm when you are ready!
Here you indicate if you are currently in the United States. This is important for your application. Click 'Yes' or 'No' as applicable. Take your time!
Please provide information about your most recent entry to the United States.
Indicate the exact date of your entry in the corresponding field.
Then, write the place where you entered the country.
Finally, select your immigration status at the time of entry and its expiration date.
Make sure all data is accurate. Thank you!
Here you should indicate if you have entered the United States on other occasions in the last five years.
If you only entered once, select 'No'. If you have entered more than once, select 'Yes' and provide the information for each entry.
Start with the most recent. For each entry, enter the date, the port of entry, and your immigration status.
Click 'Add entry' if you need to include more. Make sure all information is correct!
Please list all the jobs you have had in the last five years.
Start with the most recent.
Include positions in the U.S. and in other countries.
Gather information such as the employer's name and your occupation.
Click 'Add job' to add more positions.
Please indicate the name of the last school or college you attended.
Also select the highest educational level you completed.
Make sure to be accurate, as this information is important for your application.
Click Confirm when you're done.
Here you need to indicate the location of your school.
Please enter:

- The city where the school is located.
- The state where the school is.
- The country of the school.
Make sure the information is correct. Click Confirm when you are ready.
Here you should enter the period during which you attended school.
Indicate the start date and the end date.
It is important that these dates are accurate for your application.
Click Confirm when you are done.
Here you should list all the schools or colleges you have attended, starting with the most recent.
For each school, indicate its name in the corresponding field.
If you need to add more schools, simply click on 'Add school'.
Remember that this information is important for your asylum application. Keep going!
Please list all the places where you have lived in the last five years.
Start with the most recent address and move backward.
Click 'Add residence' to include more places if necessary.
Remember that this information is important for your application.
Here indicate if you currently live in the United States. This information is important for your application. Click the option that best describes you and then confirm your selection.
Please enter your complete current address.
This is important to keep you informed about your application.
Make sure to include street, number, city, state, and ZIP code.
Click Confirm when you are finished.
Hello, in this section, indicate if you receive mail at your current address.
You will also need to write your mailing address or P.O. Box. It’s important to ensure you receive all correspondence related to your application.
Then, click Confirm when you are done.
Indicate your current marital status. This is important for your application.
Select an option: single, married, divorced, or widowed.
Click Confirm when you are done.
Here you should indicate if you have your marriage certificate.
If you have it, please upload a copy here.
This document is important for your application.
Please indicate where you got married.
Write the city or region and the country.
You also need to provide the date of your marriage.
If you are divorced, add the date of the divorce.
Please double-check the information before confirming. Thank you!
Please write your spouse's name as it appears on their documents.
This is important for verifying your family situation.
Click Confirm when you are done.
Here you need to indicate if your spouse is currently in the United States.
If they are in the U.S., select "Yes". Otherwise, select "No".
Then, provide your spouse's current location.
This is important for your application. Click Confirm when you are done.
Here you can indicate if you have children, regardless of their age or location.
First, answer if you have children.
Then, write how many children you have in total.
This information is important for your application.
Hello! In this section, please provide your child's information.
1. Indicate the child's name.
2. Write their date of birth as it appears on their certificate.
3. Select their sex at birth.
4. Indicate their ethnicity.
5. Answer if they currently live in the United States.
6. Let us know if they have a birth certificate and upload a copy if necessary.
This information is important for your asylum application. Thank you for your attention!
Here enter the information about your father or mother.
Indicate if they are alive and their current place of residence.
We also need their names and where they were born.
This is important for your asylum application.
Click Confirm when you have completed the information.
Welcome to the section about your siblings' details!
First, let us know if you have siblings.
If the answer is yes, please write how many siblings you have.
This information is important for your application.
When you are done, click Confirm.
Hello! In this section, please fill in your sibling's information.
Provide their name and then select their gender.
Enter their date of birth as it appears on their certificate.
Then, provide your sibling's place of birth.
If they live in the United States, select "Yes" or "No."
If they live in the U.S., provide their current address.
Remember that this information is important for your application. Thank you!
Great work! You're all done with the personal information section.
Now we will work on your personal statement.
This is a very important part of your application.
You will need to provide detailed answers to specific questions about your situation and reasons for seeking asylum.
Take your time to think about your answers and be as detailed as possible.
Remember that you can change and correct anything before finishing.
If you don't have or don't remember something, continue and come back later.
It's important that everything you write or say, and the documents or other information you submit, must be true to the best of your knowledge and belief.
You can use the microphone button to record your answers, or type them out if you prefer.
When you're ready, press the 'Start' button to begin your statement.
You're almost done! Now it's time to review your application.
Take your time to carefully read all the information you provided.
Make sure everything is accurate and complete.
If you find any mistakes or need to add something, you can go back and make changes.
Remember, this is your application, and it's important that it reflects your situation correctly.
Once you're satisfied with everything, you can proceed to submit your application.
Press the 'Start' button when you're ready to begin the review process.

intro.description: We are going to ask you some specific questions about your situation and your asylum request. You will need to provide detailed answers to these questions. Remember that you can correct and change anything you need before finishing. If you don't have or don't remember something, continue and come back later. It is important to remember that everything you write or say and the documents, photos, or any other information you include or send is your responsibility to be true to the best of your knowledge and belief.

final-declaration.title: Final Declaration
final-declaration.description: I swear (affirm) that I know the contents of this application that I am signing, including all attached documents and supplements, and that they are all true to the best of my knowledge and belief. I also understand that if it is determined that I knowingly filed a frivolous asylum application, I will be permanently ineligible for any benefit under the Immigration and Nationality Act, and that I cannot avoid a finding of a frivolous application simply because someone advised me to provide false information in my asylum application.

messages.content: Fear of Return
Are you afraid to return to your country? If you have to return, are you afraid that you or your family might suffer harm or mistreatment?
Fear of returning to your country

Please explain in detail why you are afraid to return to your country. In your explanation, try to include the following information:

What harm or mistreatment you fear may happen if you return.

Who you believe might harm or mistreat you.

Whether anything has changed since you left that might affect the risk of harm or mistreatment. For example, is the situation the same, has it improved, or has it gotten worse? Please explain why.

Why you believe you could be harmed or mistreated if you return.

Any additional information that may help explain your fear of returning.
Documents related to your fear of return

Please submit any documents that may help confirm the information you have provided about your fear of returning. This may include police reports, letters, screenshots, medical records, photographs, or any other relevant documents.
Criminal History

Have you or any family member included in this application ever committed a crime or been arrested, charged, convicted, or sentenced for any offense in the United States (including violations of immigration laws)?
Details of criminal history

Provide detailed information for each instance:

What happened and under what circumstances?
When did it occur?
What was the sentence received, and what were the place and length of detention or imprisonment?
What were the reasons for the detention or conviction?
What formal charges were brought against you or your family members included in this application, and what were the reasons for your/their release?
Criminal history documents
Please submit any documents related to your or your family's criminal history. This may include court records, police reports, or any other relevant documents.
Torture
Are you afraid of being tortured in your country or in any other country to which you may be returned?
Similar to the previous question, but not only about fear of harm or mistreatment — this one is about fear of being tortured.

Please explain in detail why you are afraid that you or your family may be tortured if you return to your country. In your explanation, try to include the following information:

What you fear may happen if you return.

Who you believe might harm or torture you.

Whether anything has changed since you left that might affect this fear. For example, is the situation the same, has it improved, or has it gotten worse? Please explain why.

Why you believe you may be harmed or tortured if you return.

Any additional information that may help explain your fear of returning.
Documents related to your fear of torture

Please submit any documents that may help confirm the information you have provided about your fear of torture. This may include police reports, letters, screenshots, medical records, photographs, or any other relevant documents.

content: Your task is to collect factual information from the user about any harm, threats, or mistreatment experienced before coming to the United States.
This information will be used to help prepare a clear and complete record for the user’s asylum process in the USA.
Primary Outcomes:
- Interview the user to collect accurate facts and details.
- Build a simple timeline and fact summary.
Guidelines:
- Collect enough detail to show a clear timeline and reliable facts.
- Use follow-ups only to clarify or fill missing information (dates, places, people, reasons, outcomes).
- Do not provide legal advice, opinions, or explanations about immigration law.
- Keep questions and confirmations concise.
- Flag missing dates, contradictions, or unclear details and ask one simple question at a time to fix them.
Conversation Flow:
- One question at a time.
- Always confirm key details (who, what, when, where, how).
- Keep replies short (<80 words).
- If unclear, ask a follow-up question to clarify or fill gaps.
- Use confirmations to summarize and verify details.
- Once the user has no more information to share, you can end the interview.
Document and Evidence Handling:
- You can offer document submission whenever evidence or proof could strengthen the case.
- If the user mentions police reports, photos, letters, text messages, medical papers, or other files, tell them they can upload or attach those documents, photos, or screenshots.
I'm going to ask you a few questions about any harm, mistreatment, or threats you—or your family, close friends, or coworkers—may have experienced before coming to the United States.
When describing your experiences, please include as much detail as possible. In your explanation, try to address the following:
- What happened and how it happened.
- When it happened. Indicate whether it was a single incident or if it happened many times.
- Who was responsible. If you do not know their names, explain whether they belonged to a group, gang, cartel, political group, or were part of the government.
- Why you believe you or your family were harmed, mistreated, or threatened.
- Any additional information. Include anything else you can share that may help us better understand what happened.
If you did not experience any harm, mistreatment, or threats, just type “no” or “none,” and we’ll move to the next section.

messages.content: International Criminal History
Have you ever been arrested, charged, or convicted for a crime in any country other than the United States?
International criminal history details

Please provide details about your arrest, charge, or conviction. Include the following information:

The country where the incident occurred.

The date of the incident.

The nature of the crime.

The outcome (e.g., acquitted, convicted, case dismissed).

Any additional relevant information.
International criminal history documents
Please submit any documents related to your arrest, charge, or conviction. This may include court records, police reports, or any other relevant documents.
Memberships & Groups
Current membership and group affiliation details

Please describe in detail the current level of participation for each person who is involved:

How do they participate?

What is your or your family member’s current level of participation?

Do you or your family members currently hold leadership positions or important roles? If so, which position?

How long have you or your family member(s) participated in that organization or group?
Do you or your family continue participating in these groups or organizations?
Past membership and group affiliation details

Please provide details about your involvement with the gang or group. Include the following information:

The name of the gang or group.

The nature of your involvement.

The time period of your involvement.

Any criminal activities you were involved in.

Any additional relevant information.

Have you or any member of your family ever belonged to or been associated with any organization or group in your country of origin, such as, but not limited to, a political party, a student group, a labor union, a religious organization, a military or paramilitary group, a civil patrol, a guerrilla organization, an ethnic group, a human rights group, or the press or media?
Current membership and group affiliation documents

Please submit any documents related to you or your family's current membership or affiliation with any organization or group which may help confirm the information you have provided. This may include membership cards, letters, photographs, or any other relevant documents.
Past membership and group affiliation documents

Please submit any documents related to you or your family's past membership or affiliation with any organization or group which may help confirm the information you have provided. This may include membership cards, letters, photographs, or any other relevant documents.
Previous Applications
Have you, your spouse, your child(ren), your father, your mother, or your siblings ever applied to the United States Government for refugee status, asylum, or withholding of removal?
Details of Prior Application

What happened? Was there a decision, and if so, what was the decision?

What happened to the status that you, your spouse, your child(ren), your father, your mother, or your sibling(s) received as a result of that decision?

Were you included in the application of your father, mother, or spouse? If you were included, what was the A-Number of your father, mother, or spouse?

If an immigration judge or the Board of Immigration Appeals denied your asylum, please explain: what has changed in the conditions of your country or in your personal situation since your application was denied? Why is your case different now?
Return to Country
After you left your country to come to the United States (or the country where you suffered harm or fear harm), did you return to that country?
Explanation of travel to home country

Explain in detail:
Why did you return?
When did you return?
How long did you stay?
Documents related to travel to home country

Please submit any documents that may help confirm the information you have provided about your travel to your home country. This may include travel tickets, passport stamps, or any other relevant documents.
Participation in Persecution

Have you, your spouse, or your child(ren) ever ordered, incited, assisted, or otherwise participated in causing harm or suffering to any person because of their race, religion, nationality, membership in a particular social group, or belief in a particular political opinion?
Details of involvement
Provide a detailed description of each incident, specifying your involvement and/or the involvement of your family members.
Documents related to involvement in harm or persecution

Please submit any documents that may help confirm the information you have provided about your or your family's involvement. This may include court records, police reports, letters, or any other relevant documents.
Legal Status in Other Countries

Have you, your spouse, your child(ren), or other family members such as your father, mother, or siblings ever applied for or received any legal status in a country other than the one from which you are now requesting asylum?
Explanation of legal status in another country

Provide a detailed explanation of what happened with that legal status, for you or any of your family members. Include the following:

Where — in which country did this occur?
What was your status while you were in that country?
What was the reason you left?
Do you have the right to return with “legal residence”?
Did you apply for refugee or asylum status while living in that country? Explain why or why not.
Documents related to legal status in another country

Please submit any documents that may help confirm the information you have provided about your or your family's legal status in another country. This may include visas, residence permits, asylum or refugee status documents, or any other relevant documents.
Reasons for Asylum
Reasons for seeking asylum
Based on your previous answers and explanations, indicate the reasons you are requesting asylum. You may select one or more reasons.

For applications filed after one year of entry into the U.S., the government requires that you provide an explanation for why you did not file your application within one year of your entry.

You can also find it in notices you’ve received from the immigration office. This number is different from the Alien Number (A-number).
